messages.body_plain:
Hi Leigh,

did you check row 67330 in recordsF? From the error message it seems like that one record is causing the problems. If the date format is correct in that row, it may have to do with daylight saving time. If the date/time of that record is during the non-existent hour in which the clock is advanced from 2 to 3 am, it will be NA. In that case, adjusting the time zone helps. It is mentioned in the vignette  <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr3.html#recordTable:_tabulating_species_records>also.

Usually camera traps don't correct for DST. So if you tell the detectionHistory function that the time zone has DST (and your images ignore DST), you may end up with this problem.

For the second issue, are you using the development version of camtrapR? Even if you do, please reinstall and see if the problem persists. The error seems wrong since SR11 does not even have entries in the problem columns.

library(devtools)

install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR", ref = "dev")

Please let me know if the error persists, then I need to investigate more. In that case please feel free to share a small reproducible example.

Thank you,

Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter,
do you know why there are no date/time tags in that batch of images? Is it because of editing the images, or because you used a different camera trap model that doesn't save the date/time tag in the exif metadata (Reconyx Hyperfire HC500, I'm looking at you).
If it's because of editing with software that doesn't save metadata, there's little one can do (apart from not using that software again). I can dig up some experimental code that extracts the date/time from the data field of the image itself via optical character recognition. Alternatively, do you still have the original images? Then one could maybe write an R script that replaces the faulty images with the correct images (by filename), but one would lose the metadata tags in the process, so that's also not a good solution.

If it is because of the camera model, fixDateTimeOriginal can help. To figure out if there are usable date/time tags in the image metadata, run exifTagNames to check.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi PJ,
that's unfortunate. And the problem is that recordTable discards images without date/time information, so you can't simply export them without the date/time tag (unless you're willing to modify the recordTable function, which may break in several places if it is given images without date/times). So you may need to do it manually.

Were the images renamed with imageRename?

Here's a somewhat hacky solution that accesses the digiKam database, pulls a table of images (with tags) from there, and then parses the filenames to extract date/time. It assumes images were renamed with imageRename.
It abuses several internal functions normally used by recordTable (partly written and intended for video files) and adds some extra stuff,, but it seems to work. You need to change the directories of course.

# access digiKam database
digiKamTablesList <- camtrapR:::accessDigiKamDatabase (db_directory = "C:/Users/Juergen/Pictures",   # database directory
                                  db_filename = "digikam4.db")

# get image table for a certain camera trap station
stationDir <- "C:/Users/Juergen/Pictures/camtrapR/sample_images_species_tagged/StationA"

digiKam_image_table <- camtrapR:::digiKamVideoHierarchicalSubject(stationDir = stationDir,
                                            digiKamTablesList,    # output of accessDigiKamDatabase
                                            videoFormat = "jpg"          # character vector of desired video formats
)

filenames_example <- digiKam_image_table$name

# parse filenames and create data frame (one for each image)
list_filenames_analysed <- lapply(filenames_example , FUN = function(filename){

  filename_split <- unlist(strsplit(filename, split = "__"))

  out <- data.frame(Station = filename_split[1],
                    Date = filename_split[2],
                    Time = gsub(pattern = "-",
                                replacement = ":",
                                substr(filename_split[3],
                                       start = 1, stop = 8)),
                    FileName = filename)

  out$DateTimeOriginal = paste(out$Date, out$Time)
  return(out)
})

# combine into one data frame
df_datetime_from_filenames <- do.call( "rbind", list_filenames_analysed)

# combine with digiKam output
image_table <- cbind(digiKam_image_table, df_datetime_from_filenames)

The output contains a lot of stuff from digiKam still, but you can clean it up and get something like a record table.

You'll still need to parse the HierarchicalSubject field though:

image_table2 <- camtrapR:::addMetadataAsColumns (intable                    = image_table,
                                                 metadata.tagname           = "HierarchicalSubject",
                                                 metadataHierarchyDelimitor = "|",
                                                 multiple_tag_separator     = "_&_")

osoind <- recordTableIndividual (...)   # as above

Hi Christian,
which version of camtrapR are you using? It seems like a bug, and a few other people also pointed out issues with date/time columns. Some of the issues are fixed in the development version on github, so you may want to give that a try:
library(devtools)

And the problem is that recordTable discards images without date/time information, so you can't simply export them without the date/time tag (unless you're willing to modify the recordTable function, which may break in several places if it is given images without date/times). So you may need to do it manually.
>
> Were the images renamed with imageRename?
>
> Here's a somewhat hacky solution that accesses the digiKam database, pulls a table of images (with tags) from there, and then parses the filenames to extract date/time. It assumes images were renamed with imageRename.
> It abuses several internal functions normally used by recordTable (partly written and intended for video files) and adds some extra stuff,, but it seems to work. You need to change the directories of course.
>
> # access digiKam database
> digiKamTablesList <- camtrapR:::accessDigiKamDatabase (db_directory = "C:/Users/Juergen/Pictures",   # database directory
>                                   db_filename = "digikam4.db")
>
>
> # get image table for a certain camera trap station
> stationDir <- "C:/Users/Juergen/Pictures/camtrapR/sample_images_species_tagged/StationA"
>
> digiKam_image_table <- camtrapR:::digiKamVideoHierarchicalSubject(stationDir = stationDir,
>                                             digiKamTablesList,    # output of accessDigiKamDatabase
>                                             videoFormat = "jpg"          # character vector of desired video formats
> )
>
>
> filenames_example <- digiKam_image_table$name
>
> # parse filenames and create data frame (one for each image)
> list_filenames_analysed <- lapply(filenames_example , FUN = function(filename){
>
>   filename_split <- unlist(strsplit(filename, split = "__"))
>
>   out <- data.frame(Station = filename_split[1],
>                     Date = filename_split[2],
>                     Time = gsub(pattern = "-",
>                                 replacement = ":",
>                                 substr(filename_split[3],
>                                        start = 1, stop = 8)),
>                     FileName = filename)
>
>   out$DateTimeOriginal = paste(out$Date, out$Time)
>   return(out)
> })
>
>
> # combine into one data frame
> df_datetime_from_filenames <- do.call( "rbind", list_filenames_analysed)
>
> # combine with digiKam output
